chunks: And what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿAbdī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from his brother, from his father ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام about salat (prayer) between the graves: is it valid? He said: There is no objection.

So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we understand them to mean that this is when there is a barrier between him and the grave, or when there are ten cubits between him and the grave, according to what he explained in the first report.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship under discussion
key_terms.الْخَبَرِ الْأَوَّلِ: the first report, which provides further detail
key_terms.الْقُبُورِ: the graves, the location relevant to the ruling
key_terms.حَائِلٌ: a barrier separating the worshipper from the grave
key_terms.عَشَرَةُ أَذْرُعٍ: ten cubits, a specified minimum distance
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) between graves permissible in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling of performing salat (prayer) between graves and indicates that it is not objectionable in itself. The reconciliation given explains that permissibility applies when there is a barrier or sufficient distance between the worshipper and the grave, showing a juristic method of harmonizing reports.
